In this paper we analyze quiver gauge theories arising from D-branes at singularities that include fractional branes of the dynamical supersymmetry breaking (DSB) type. These are configurations whose low-energy dynamics is such that no supersymmetric ground states survive at the classical level, the quiver theory being driven instead toward a genuinely non-supersymmetric infrared regime. The removal of classical vacua by strong dynamics is a hallmark of this class of fractional branes, and understanding the resulting vacuum structure is central to connecting brane constructions with dynamical supersymmetry breaking scenarios.

We show that by introducing flavors into these quiver theories—realized geometrically by adding extra non-compact branes to the brane configuration—one generates local, meta-stable supersymmetry breaking minima. The structure of these vacua is strikingly similar to that found in the ISS-type construction of SQCD with massive flavors, where a rank condition on the mass matrix of the auxiliary fields forces a non-supersymmetric ground state that is nonetheless a stable local minimum of the effective potential, protected by a parametrically large barrier from any supersymmetric vacua that may exist far away in field space. This parallel suggests that the mechanism responsible for meta-stable breaking in these quiver gauge theories is closely tied to the same physics that underlies the SQCD examples, translated into the language of branes and quivers.

A central technical result of this work is a direct method for computing the masses of the pseudomoduli fields using Feynman diagram techniques. In these constructions, the tree-level potential typically possesses accidental flat directions—pseudomoduli—that are not protected by any symmetry and are consequently lifted only at one loop, through the Coleman-Weinberg mechanism. Determining whether these lifted directions correspond to a genuine local minimum (rather than a saddle point or maximum) generally requires evaluating the one-loop effective potential and extracting the mass matrix for the pseudomoduli, a task that can be computationally intensive when the classical superpotential involves several fields and coupling constants. We show that this analysis can be considerably streamlined by computing the pseudomoduli masses directly through appropriate Feynman diagrams, bypassing the need to construct and expand the full Coleman-Weinberg potential.

This diagrammatic approach not only simplifies existing calculations but also enables us to obtain fully analytic results for the pseudomoduli masses across all the DSB-brane models under consideration. In particular, it extends and generalizes the results previously obtained for the dP1 (first del Pezzo) quiver theory in earlier work, where the one-loop pseudomoduli masses were computed for that specific example. The techniques developed here apply uniformly to any quiver gauge theory built from an arbitrary configuration of DSB fractional branes, and they hold for generic values of the superpotential couplings, without restriction to special points in parameter space. This generality allows for a systematic and efficient exploration of meta-stable supersymmetry breaking vacua in a broad class of brane-engineered gauge theories, providing further evidence for the ubiquity of such meta-stable states in string-theoretic realizations of dynamical supersymmetry breaking.

# Quiver Gauge Theories with Dynamical Supersymmetry Breaking and Metastable Vacua from Flavor Branes

Dynamical supersymmetry breaking (DSB) provides one of the most compelling mechanisms for generating hierarchies in particle physics models derived from string theory, and D-brane constructions at singular geometries offer a natural framework for realizing such phenomena in quiver gauge theories. In this paper, we investigate a broad class of quiver gauge theories arising from D-branes probing Calabi-Yau singularities that are known to exhibit dynamical supersymmetry breaking, and we study the effect of introducing additional matter content through non-compact "flavor" branes.

The addition of these flavor branes modifies the low-energy gauge theory by introducing new chiral multiplets charged under the gauge groups of the quiver, playing a role analogous to the massive flavors in the Intriligator-Seiberg-Shih (ISS) construction of metastable supersymmetry breaking in supersymmetric QCD. Just as in the ISS scenario, where the introduction of massive fundamental flavors into SQCD with a dynamically generated superpotential leads to the appearance of long-lived metastable vacua that spontaneously break supersymmetry, we demonstrate that a similar mechanism operates generically in these brane-engineered quiver theories. The flavor branes source new terms in the effective superpotential, and the resulting F-term equations admit a rich vacuum structure that includes local minima where supersymmetry is broken while remaining parametrically separated from the supersymmetric vacua of the theory. These metastable vacua are shown to be a robust feature of the construction, persisting across the enlarged family of quiver models considered here.

A central technical challenge in establishing the metastability of such vacua is to verify that the pseudomoduli space—flat directions that appear at tree level due to the classical vacuum degeneracy—is stabilized once quantum corrections are taken into account. In the class of theories considered, the classical potential typically exhibits large moduli spaces of degenerate vacua, and one must compute the one-loop Coleman-Weinberg effective potential to determine whether these directions are lifted to positive mass-squared values, thereby confirming the local stability of the supersymmetry-breaking vacuum. Historically, such computations have been performed on a largely case-by-case basis, often relying on explicit diagonalization of mass matrices and direct evaluation of the supertrace formula, a procedure that becomes increasingly cumbersome as the complexity of the quiver and its associated superpotential grows.

To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a new, efficient method based on Feynman diagram techniques for computing the one-loop pseudomoduli masses in a wide class of theories with calculable DSB sectors. By organizing the relevant loop contributions in terms of a small set of diagrams built from the interactions dictated by the superpotential, we derive compact analytic expressions for the pseudomoduli mass matrix that depend only on the general structure of the quiver—namely the ranks of the gauge groups, the matter content, and the superpotential couplings—rather than on the details of any specific model. This diagrammatic approach not only streamlines the calculation but also makes manifest the origin of the mass terms in terms of specific holomorphic couplings, providing valuable physical insight into which interactions are responsible for stabilizing the pseudomoduli.

We apply this new technique to a variety of quiver gauge theories obtained by adding flavor branes to known DSB brane configurations, systematically confirming the existence of metastable supersymmetry-breaking vacua and explicitly computing the resulting pseudomoduli spectra. In particular, our method reproduces and generalizes earlier results obtained for the specific case of the first del Pezzo ($dP_1$) quiver gauge theory, where metastable supersymmetry breaking was previously demonstrated through more laborious means. By extending the analysis to an entire class of related quiver theories with arbitrary superpotential couplings, we show that the phenomenon of metastable supersymmetry breaking induced by flavor branes is a generic and calculable feature of this broad family of brane constructions, rather than an isolated property of a single example. Our results thus provide both a unifying framework for understanding dynamical supersymmetry breaking in quiver gauge theories and a powerful computational tool for exploring the vacuum structure of a wide range of string-theoretic constructions relevant to model building beyond the Standard Model.

# Dynamical Supersymmetry Breaking in SQCD: A Feynman Diagram Perspective

Dynamical supersymmetry breaking (DSB) represents one of the most compelling mechanisms for generating hierarchies in particle physics, offering an elegant alternative to explicit supersymmetry breaking. Supersymmetric Quantum Chromodynamics (SQCD) serves as a paradigmatic framework for studying these phenomena, providing a controlled setting where the interplay between gauge dynamics and supersymmetry can be analyzed with remarkable precision.

## The Basic Framework

SQCD extends ordinary QCD by introducing squarks and gluinos as superpartners to quarks and gluons, organizing these fields into chiral and vector supermultiplets. The theory is characterized by the gauge group SU(N) with N_f flavors of matter in the fundamental representation. The vacuum structure of this theory depends critically on the ratio N_f/N, leading to a rich phase diagram that includes regions of confinement, Seiberg duality, and—crucially—dynamical supersymmetry breaking.

## Mechanisms of DSB

Unlike explicit breaking introduced by soft terms, dynamical breaking arises from nonperturbative effects—typically instanton contributions or strong gauge dynamics—that generate a superpotential dynamically. In SQCD, when N_f < N, gaugino condensation and instanton effects can generate an effective superpotential that lifts the moduli space and breaks supersymmetry spontaneously. The Affleck-Dine-Seiberg superpotential is the archetypal example, arising from instanton calculations in theories with N_f = N - 1.

## Feynman Diagram Techniques in Nonperturbative Analysis

While DSB is fundamentally a nonperturbative phenomenon, Feynman diagram techniques remain indispensable tools for understanding the underlying physics:

**Perturbative Matching**: Feynman diagrams calculated in the weakly coupled regime allow theorists to match onto the effective low-energy description, verifying consistency between microscopic and macroscopic descriptions of the theory.

**Instanton Calculations**: The computation of instanton-generated superpotentials relies heavily on evaluating fermion zero modes and bosonic fluctuations around instanton backgrounds—calculations that borrow extensively from Feynman diagrammatic methods, including the saddle-point evaluation of path integrals.

**Anomaly Analysis**: Feynman diagrams computing triangle anomalies are essential for verifying 't Hooft anomaly matching conditions, which provide crucial consistency checks on proposed dual descriptions of strongly coupled SQCD.

**Two-Loop and Higher-Order Corrections**: Even in regimes where nonperturbative effects dominate, higher-loop Feynman diagram calculations help establish the reliability of holomorphic quantities protected by supersymmetric non-renormalization theorems.

## Physical Implications

The synthesis of DSB mechanisms with rigorous perturbative and semiclassical techniques in SQCD has profound implications for model building beyond the Standard Model. These theories provide templates for constructing hidden sectors where supersymmetry breaking occurs dynamically, generating naturally small scales through dimensional transmutation—analogous to how Λ_QCD arises in ordinary QCD.

## Conclusion

The study of dynamical supersymmetry breaking in SQCD exemplifies the productive tension between perturbative and nonperturbative methods in quantum field theory. Feynman diagrams, despite their inherently perturbative origin, continue to illuminate the path toward understanding these deeply nonperturbative phenomena, whether through direct calculation, consistency checks, or matching procedures that bridge the gap between weak and strong coupling regimes. This interplay remains central to ongoing efforts in both formal theoretical development and phenomenological model building.

# Abstract

We study metastable supersymmetry breaking vacua arising in quiver gauge theories engineered from D-branes at Calabi-Yau singularities, focusing on configurations that combine fractional branes with flavor D-branes. Building on the Intriligator-Seiberg-Shih mechanism, we show that adding flavor branes to fractional brane setups on toric singularities generically induces long-lived metastable vacua that break supersymmetry dynamically, while the true supersymmetric ground state is separated by a parametrically large distance in field space. We analyze the resulting quiver gauge theories in the regime where a subset of nodes flows to a magnetic description with massive flavors, showing that rank conditions naturally break supersymmetry through rank mismatches analogous to the ISS scenario, and we identify the pseudomoduli space and its one-loop lifting via the Coleman-Weinberg potential. The gravity dual perspective is discussed: flavor branes correspond to additional sources wrapping non-compact cycles, and the metastable vacuum is interpreted in terms of anti-branes or brane/antibrane configurations polarizing in the dual geometry, with the decay rate to the supersymmetric vacuum controlled by the separation between the branes in the internal space. We work out several explicit examples, including the conifold and its orbifolds/deformations, computing the matter content, superpotential, and lifetime of the metastable vacua as functions of the number of fractional and flavor branes. Our results provide a systematic string-theoretic embedding of dynamical supersymmetry breaking and suggest a broad class of brane constructions relevant for model building of low-scale supersymmetry breaking and mediation to the visible sector.

# Abstract

We study the effects of adding flavors to a class of brane quiver gauge theories arising from D-branes at Calabi-Yau singularities that exhibit dynamical supersymmetry breaking (DSB) in the sense of Intriligator-Seiberg-Shih (ISS). Building on the analysis of the del Pezzo one (dP1) quiver gauge theory, where the addition of flavor branes was shown to generate a metastable, long-lived vacuum with broken supersymmetry, we extend this construction to a broader family of quiver theories obtained from D-branes probing toric Calabi-Yau threefold singularities. 

We show that the mechanism responsible for supersymmetry breaking in the dP1 case—namely, the interplay between the rank-deficient Seiberg dual description and the ISS-type metastable vacua arising from the addition of massive flavors—persists across this generalized set of geometries. In particular, we identify the conditions on the quiver structure, superpotential couplings, and choice of fractional branes under which the introduction of flavor branes (realized geometrically as noncompact D-branes wrapping additional cycles) reproduces the ISS mechanism at the level of the effective low-energy gauge theory. We construct the corresponding meta-stable vacua explicitly, compute the pseudo-moduli space and one-loop Coleman-Weinberg potential, and verify that supersymmetry is broken at tree level while the resulting non-supersymmetric vacuum remains parametrically long-lived compared to the dynamically generated scale.

Our results demonstrate that metastable supersymmetry breaking of the ISS type is a generic and robust feature of flavored D-brane quiver gauge theories at Calabi-Yau singularities, extending well beyond the original dP1 example. This provides further evidence that string theoretic embeddings of dynamical supersymmetry breaking through metastable vacua are ubiquitous in the landscape of quiver gauge theories, with potential applications to moduli stabilization and gauge mediation scenarios in string phenomenology.

We compute one-loop masses for pseudomoduli in quiver gauge theories arising from fractional branes at del Pezzo singularities, employing diagrammatic methods based on the Coleman-Weinberg effective potential. Building on previous results for the dP1 (also known as F0-related) geometry, we extend the analysis to a broader class of toric del Pezzo quiver gauge theories, systematically identifying the pseudomoduli directions associated with supersymmetry-breaking metastable vacua and determining their lifted masses through explicit Feynman diagram calculations. # Abstract

We study metastable vacua in flavored quiver gauge theories arising from D-brane constructions that incorporate dynamical supersymmetry breaking (DSB) branes. By engineering brane configurations that combine quiver gauge groups with flavor branes and fractional branes responsible for supersymmetry breaking, we construct a class of models generalizing the Intriligator-Seiberg-Shih (ISS) scenario to quiver gauge theories with bifundamental matter. We analyze the vacuum structure of these theories in the magnetic dual description, where the interplay between the quiver structure and the massive flavors gives rise to long-lived metastable supersymmetry-breaking vacua alongside the supersymmetric vacua expected from Seiberg duality.

We demonstrate that the low-energy effective description of these brane setups reduces, under suitable decoupling limits, to product gauge groups of SQCD-like theories with massive flavors, each exhibiting a rank condition mechanism for supersymmetry breaking similar to the original ISS construction. We compute the pseudo-moduli space and the one-loop Coleman-Weinberg potential for the quiver theory, identifying the conditions under which the metastable minimum is parametrically long-lived compared to the scale of supersymmetry restoration. Particular attention is paid to comparing the vacuum energies, lifetimes, and moduli spaces of the quiver models to the ordinary SQCD case, highlighting how the additional gauge and flavor structure of the quiver modifies the R-symmetry breaking pattern and the multiplicity of metastable states.

Our results show that DSB brane constructions naturally accommodate multiple sectors of dynamical supersymmetry breaking that can be simultaneously realized within a single string-derived quiver gauge theory, offering a geometric and brane-theoretic origin for metastable vacua in more general gauge theories beyond simple SQCD. These findings suggest possible applications to model building for gauge mediation of supersymmetry breaking, where quiver structures may provide additional flavor and messenger sectors emerging directly from the brane construction.

## Abstract

We present analytic methods for computing one-loop pseudomodulus masses in dynamical supersymmetry breaking (DSB) theories arising from D-brane quiver gauge theories with added flavors. Building on the Coleman-Weinberg formalism adapted to the pseudo-flat directions characteristic of metastable supersymmetry-breaking vacua, we develop techniques that exploit the quiver structure—encoding gauge group factors, bifundamental matter, and superpotential couplings—to systematically organize the computation of the one-loop scalar and fermion mass spectra. Rather than resorting to case-by-case numerical diagonalization of the Coleman-Weinberg potential's Hessian, our approach derives closed-form expressions for pseudomodulus masses in terms of the quiver's combinatorial data (ranks, arrow multiplicities, and superpotential coefficients), making the parametric dependence of the mass spectrum on flavor number and rank assignments transparent. We apply these methods to a broad class of brane quiver realizations of DSB models—including generalizations of the ISS-type and rank-deficient meson-deformed theories—that arise from D-branes at singularities, showing how varying flavor content shifts the pseudomodulus masses and affects the stability of the metastable vacuum. The resulting formulas provide efficient diagnostic tools for verifying the perturbative stability (absence of tachyonic directions) of pseudomoduli in a wide range of quiver-based DSB constructions, and clarify how flavor deformations of the quiver control the interplay between R-symmetry breaking, moduli lifting, and metastability. These techniques are broadly applicable to the systematic study of metastable dynamical supersymmetry breaking in string-derived quiver gauge theories.
